questions.question: Derive Lawrence's expression for the time t for a particle of charge q and mass m to complete one circular path in a uniform magnetic field of flux density B.
questions.answer: t = 2 pi m / (B q)
steps: The magnetic force provides the centripetal force: B q v = m v^2 / r.
Rearrange to get the radius: r = m v / (B q).
The time for one circuit is the circumference divided by the speed: t = 2 pi r / v.
Substitute r: t = 2 pi (m v / (B q)) / v, so the speed cancels.
Result: t = 2 pi m / (B q), independent of speed and radius.

questions.question: Explain the significance of the expression t = 2 pi m / (B q) for the operation of a cyclotron that uses an alternating potential difference.
questions.answer: The period does not depend on speed, so a fixed-frequency a.c. supply stays in step with the particles as they speed up.
steps: The period t = 2 pi m / (B q) is the same for every orbit radius and speed.
So the frequency f = 1/t = B q / (2 pi m) is constant for a given particle.
Setting the a.c. p.d. to this frequency means the field reverses each time the particle reaches a gap.
The particle is accelerated in every gap crossing, so its energy increases as it spirals outward.
Without a constant period, the particles would fall out of step with the field.

questions.question: A proton is accelerated from rest to 1.5 x 10^7 m s^-1 in a cyclotron with B = 1.6 T and accelerating p.d. 13 kV. Find the time taken.
questions.answer: Time = 1.9 x 10^-6 s
steps: Kinetic energy gained: E k = 0.5 m v^2 = 0.5 x 1.67 x 10^-27 x (1.5 x 10^7)^2 = 1.88 x 10^-13 J (proton mass 1.67 x 10^-27 kg, standard value).
Energy gained per gap crossing: q V = 1.6 x 10^-19 x 13 000 = 2.08 x 10^-15 J.
Number of gap crossings: N = 1.88 x 10^-13 / 2.08 x 10^-15 = 90.3.
Period: t = 2 pi m / (B q) = 4.10 x 10^-8 s, so one crossing occurs every half period, 2.05 x 10^-8 s.

questions.question: Explain why high energy particles are needed to investigate the structure of nucleons.
questions.answer: High energy gives a short de Broglie wavelength, so the probe can resolve detail as small as the nucleon.
steps: A probe can only reveal structure about as small as its wavelength.
The de Broglie wavelength is lambda = h / p.
High energy means high momentum, so the wavelength is short.
A short wavelength (about the size of a nucleon or smaller) is needed to resolve quarks inside nucleons.
High energy also provides the energy to overcome forces and to create new particles.

questions.question: Name and describe the process by which electrons are produced by the heated filament of an electron gun.
questions.answer: Thermionic emission: the heated filament gives electrons enough thermal energy to escape from its surface.
steps: The process is thermionic emission.
The filament is heated, so the free electrons in the metal gain kinetic energy.
Electrons with enough energy to overcome the work function of the metal escape from the surface.

questions.question: An electron enters a linac at 2.5 x 10^6 m s^-1 and passes through 60 drift tubes, each step with a p.d. of 80 kV. Find its energy as it emerges.
questions.answer: Energy = 4.8 MeV (about 7.7 x 10^-13 J)
steps: Energy gained at each step: q V = 1.6 x 10^-19 x 80 000 = 1.28 x 10^-14 J (80 keV).
Total energy gained over 60 steps: 60 x 80 keV = 4.8 MeV.
Initial kinetic energy: 0.5 x 9.11 x 10^-31 x (2.5 x 10^6)^2 = 2.8 x 10^-18 J, which is only about 18 eV and negligible.

questions.question: Explain why successive drift tubes of a linac have the same length for very high energy electrons.
questions.answer: At very high energies the electrons move at almost constant (near light) speed, so equal lengths give equal times in each tube.
steps: The time spent in each drift tube must equal half the period of the a.c. supply.
For very high energy electrons the speed is almost the speed of light and changes very little.
Equal lengths therefore give nearly equal transit times, matching the fixed a.c. frequency.

questions.question: Explain how a standing wave is produced in the linac.
questions.answer: Two waves of the same frequency and amplitude travelling in opposite directions superpose to form a standing wave.
steps: An incident wave travels along the linac in one direction.
It is reflected at the end, so a wave of the same frequency travels back the other way.
The two waves superpose and interfere.
At some points they reinforce (antinodes) and at others they cancel (nodes), forming a stationary pattern.

questions.question: Electrons of energy 2.5 keV follow a path of radius 61 mm when rotated by magnets through 270 degrees. Find the magnetic flux density.
steps: Kinetic energy: E k = 2.5 x 10^3 x 1.6 x 10^-19 = 4.0 x 10^-16 J.
The magnetic force provides the centripetal force: B q v = m v^2 / r, so B = m v / (q r).
The 270 degree turn only sets how far the beam is turned; the radius and field give the answer.

questions.question: Give a reason why radon atoms do not leave tracks in a cloud chamber.
questions.answer: Radon atoms are neutral and do not ionise the vapour; tracks come from ionising charged particles.
steps: Tracks form where a particle ionises the supersaturated vapour along its path.
A neutral radon atom does not ionise the vapour, so it leaves no visible trail.

questions.question: Complete the nuclear equations for radon decaying by alpha emission to polonium, which decays by alpha emission to lead.
steps: Alpha particles are helium nuclei, 4/2 He, so each decay reduces the mass number by 4 and the proton number by 2.
Radon-222 (proton number 86) gives polonium with mass number 218 and proton number 84, plus an alpha particle.
Polonium-218 gives lead with mass number 214 and proton number 82, plus an alpha particle.
Radon-222 is the standard isotope for this chain; the mass numbers are checked by conservation.

questions.question: Sketch a vector diagram showing the momenta of the two alpha particles and the lead ion after radon decay, with the tracks at 60 degrees.
questions.answer: Pending: the answer is a sketch, which cannot be given in text. The lead momentum vector must equal the negative of the vector sum of the two alpha momenta.

questions.question: The radon atom was stationary. The two alpha particles move at 1.74 x 10^7 and 1.81 x 10^7 m s^-1 with 60 degrees between their tracks. The lead ion has mass 3.52 x 10^-25 kg. Find the speed of the lead ion.
questions.answer: Speed of lead ion = 5.8 x 10^5 m s^-1
steps: The initial momentum is zero, so the lead ion momentum equals minus the vector sum of the two alpha momenta.
Resultant of the alpha momenta with 60 degrees between them: p^2 = p1^2 + p2^2 + 2 p1 p2 cos 60 = 4.17 x 10^-38 N^2 s^2.
So p = 2.04 x 10^-19 N s, which is the magnitude of the lead ion momentum.

questions.question: A photograph shows another pair of alpha tracks after radon decay. Deduce which track belongs to the first alpha particle emitted.

questions.question: Which is the reason high energies are required to investigate the structure of nucleons with electrons? A: to create new particles; B: to overcome repulsive electrostatic forces; C: relativistic increase in lifetime; D: to produce short de Broglie wavelengths.
questions.answer: D: to produce short de Broglie wavelengths
steps: Resolving structure needs a short wavelength, since lambda = h / p.
Higher energy gives higher momentum and a shorter de Broglie wavelength.
Option A and B are side effects, and C is not a real reason, so D is correct.

questions.question: Which change would increase the energy transferred to a charged particle as it travels through 360 degrees in a cyclotron? A: increase distance between dees; B: increase frequency of p.d.; C: increase magnetic field strength; D: increase maximum p.d. across dees.
questions.answer: D: increasing the maximum potential difference across the dees
steps: Energy is gained only in the gap between the dees, once per half turn.
Energy gained per crossing is q V, so the energy gained in one full turn (two crossings) is 2 q V.
Raising the maximum p.d. increases the energy gained per crossing.
The magnetic field and frequency change the orbit timing and radius, not the energy gained per crossing.

questions.question: Which is the reason the drift tubes of a linac have increasing length? A: so the p.d. has a constant frequency; B: so the particle gains the same energy in each tube; C: so the p.d. increases each tube; D: so the time in each tube increases.
questions.answer: A: so that the p.d. can have a constant frequency
steps: The particle speeds up along the linac, so each tube must be longer to keep the time in it equal to half the a.c. period.
This lets a single fixed-frequency a.c. supply match the particle at every gap.
Option A states this reason; B, C and D are not the reason for the length change.

questions.question: In a cyclotron, which quantity increases as the radius of the spiral path increases? A: frequency of the a.c. p.d.; B: magnetic flux density; C: p.d. between the dees; D: velocity of the particles.
questions.answer: D: the velocity of the charged particles
steps: The radius of the path is r = m v / (B q).
For a fixed B, q and m, the radius is proportional to velocity.
So an increase in radius means an increase in velocity; option D is correct.

questions.question: Electrons can be used to probe the nuclei of atoms. Which best explains this? A: electrons can be accelerated to very high energies; B: electrons can be deflected by a magnetic field; C: electrons can be part of an atom; D: electrons can be released by thermionic emission.
questions.answer: A: electrons can be accelerated to very high energies
steps: To probe a nucleus the electron needs a very short de Broglie wavelength.
A short wavelength requires very high momentum, which needs very high energy.
Option A gives this reason; the other options do not explain probing nuclei.

questions.question: Ions travel in a straight line at 5.0 x 10^5 m s^-1 in a velocity selector with electric field strength 10 500 N C^-1. Find the magnetic flux density.
steps: Straight-line motion means the electric and magnetic forces balance: q E = q v B.
So B = E / v.

questions.question: Explain why the detector in a mass spectrometer detects only one isotope of oxygen when all ions have the same velocity and enter a uniform magnetic field.
questions.answer: Radius r = m v / (B q): with equal v, B and q, only one mass gives the radius that reaches the detector.
steps: The ions have the same velocity after the selector, and the field is uniform.
In the magnetic field the radius is r = m v / (B q), so the radius depends on mass.
Different isotopes have different masses and therefore different radii.
Only the isotope whose radius matches the detector position reaches it.

questions.question: A particle detector shows tracks of two particles X and Y produced by the decay of a kaon at O. Which conclusion can be drawn from the tracks? A: field into page; B: X positive; C: Y is an electron; D: X and Y opposite charge.

questions.question: Show that the speed v of electrons passing undeflected between plates separated by distance d, with p.d. V and magnetic flux density B, is v = V / (B d).
questions.answer: v = V / (B d)
steps: The electric field between the plates is E = V / d.
Forces balance for a straight-line path: e E = e v B.
Substitute E: e (V / d) = e v B.
Cancel e and rearrange: v = V / (B d).

questions.question: Show that the electron speed was about 3 x 10^7 m s^-1 with V = 231 V, d = 1.5 cm and B = 5.5 x 10^-4 T.
steps: Use v = V / (B d).
Convert d: 1.5 cm = 0.015 m.

questions.question: With the electric field switched off, electrons move in a circle of radius 39 cm in B = 5.5 x 10^-4 T. Using v = 2.8 x 10^7 m s^-1 from the previous part, deduce whether e/m from this experiment is consistent with the accepted 1.8 x 10^11 C kg^-1.
questions.answer: e/m = 1.3 x 10^11 C kg^-1, which is not consistent with 1.8 x 10^11 C kg^-1 (about 27 percent lower).
steps: For circular motion: B e v = m v^2 / r, so e/m = v / (B r).
This differs from 1.8 x 10^11 C kg^-1 by about 27 percent, so the values are not consistent.

questions.question: Explain how the electron diffraction pattern from thin metal films changed scientists' understanding of the nature of electrons.
questions.answer: The pattern shows electrons diffract and interfere, so electrons have wave properties as well as being particles.
steps: Diffraction and interference patterns are a property of waves.
Electrons passing through thin metal film produce such a pattern.
This shows that electrons behave as waves (wave-particle duality), with de Broglie wavelength lambda = h / p.

questions.question: Explain the use of electric fields in a linac, referring to the frequency of the a.c. supply.
questions.answer: Electric fields in the gaps accelerate particles each time the a.c. field reverses; the frequency matches the particle transit time in each tube.
steps: Electric fields exist only in the gaps between drift tubes, where they accelerate the particles.
Inside the drift tubes the field is shielded, so particles move at constant speed.
The a.c. supply reverses the field each half cycle, so the field points forward at each gap when the particle arrives.
The supply frequency is constant, so each tube length is set so the particle spends half a period in it.
The particle gains energy at each gap, so its speed increases along the linac.

questions.question: Explain why a magnetic field is applied at right angles to the dees in a cyclotron.
questions.answer: The magnetic force acts at right angles to the velocity and provides the centripetal force that keeps particles on a circular path.
steps: A force perpendicular to velocity does no work and changes only direction.
The magnetic force F = B q v acts at right angles to the velocity.
This provides the centripetal force that keeps the particle moving in a circle inside the dees.

questions.question: Which statement is NOT a reason why particles with high energy are required to investigate nucleon structure? A: to overcome forces between particles; B: to ensure particles have very high momentum; C: to ensure a very small de Broglie wavelength; D: to produce new particles.
questions.answer: B: to ensure particles have a very high momentum
steps: A: overcoming forces needs high energy, so it is a reason.
C: a small de Broglie wavelength needs high momentum, so it is a reason.
D: producing new particles needs energy, so it is a reason.
B is the consequence rather than the purpose: high momentum is not itself the reason, so it is the statement that is not a reason.

questions.question: Using the proton momentum of about 5 x 10^-20 N s and alpha particle momenta 1.26 x 10^-19 and 8.06 x 10^-20 N s (alpha mass 6.64 x 10^-27 kg), deduce whether the collision was elastic.
questions.answer: Kinetic energy before is about 1.20 x 10^-12 J and after is about 1.24 x 10^-12 J, so the collision is elastic within the precision of the data.
steps: Elastic collisions conserve kinetic energy, where E k = p^2 / (2 m).
After, proton (mass 1.67 x 10^-27 kg, standard value): (5 x 10^-20)^2 / (2 x 1.67 x 10^-27) = 7.5 x 10^-13 J.
Total after = 1.24 x 10^-12 J, which equals the initial value within the rounding of the momenta, so the collision is elastic.

questions.question: Why do the tubes of a linac get progressively longer along its length? A: frequency decreases; B: frequency increases; C: particles gain mass; D: particles spend the same time in each tube.
questions.answer: D: the particles must spend the same time in each tube
steps: The a.c. supply has a constant frequency, so each half period is the same.
Each tube must be traversed in one half period for the field to reverse correctly.
As the particles speed up, the tubes must be longer so the time in each stays equal; option D is correct.

questions.question: Which statement is true for a cyclotron? A: it can accelerate neutrons; B: it uses a magnetic field to increase speed; C: it uses an alternating p.d. at constant frequency; D: it uses an electric field to keep particles in a circle.
questions.answer: C: a cyclotron uses an alternating potential difference at a constant frequency
steps: Neutrons are uncharged, so they cannot be accelerated by electric or magnetic fields (A is false).
The magnetic field changes direction only, and does not change speed (B is false).
The electric field is provided by an alternating p.d. at a constant frequency matching the cyclotron frequency (C is true).
The magnetic field, not the electric field, keeps particles in a circle (D is false).

questions.question: Calculate the velocity of electrons that would cause green light of wavelength 560 nm to be emitted from an oxygen atom.
steps: The electron's kinetic energy must supply the photon energy: E = h c / lambda.
Kinetic energy: 0.5 m v^2 = E, so v = sqrt(2 E / m).
This assumes all the electron kinetic energy is transferred to the oxygen atom.

questions.question: An electron of speed 1650 km s^-1 moves perpendicular to B = 48 T and emits radio waves at its rotation frequency. Calculate the radius and deduce whether this would interfere with a 220 m radio station.
questions.answer: Radius = 2.0 x 10^-7 m; emitted frequency = 1.3 x 10^12 Hz, far from the 1.4 x 10^6 Hz of the station, so no interference.
steps: Radius from B q v = m v^2 / r: r = m v / (B q).
Rotation frequency: f = v / (2 pi r) = B q / (2 pi m).
Station frequency: f = c / lambda = 3.0 x 10^8 / 220 = 1.4 x 10^6 Hz.
The frequencies differ by about six orders of magnitude, so there is no interference.

questions.question: Which is the reason high energies are needed for high energy electrons to investigate nucleon structure? A: to cause annihilation; B: to produce individual quarks; C: to produce short de Broglie wavelengths; D: to overcome repulsive electrostatic forces.
questions.answer: C: to produce short de Broglie wavelengths
steps: Investigating structure requires a short wavelength probe, lambda = h / p.
Short wavelength needs high momentum, so high energy.
Option C gives this reason; annihilation and quark production are results, not the reason for high energy.

questions.question: A ball accelerates uniformly across a 2.0 cm gap in 0.22 s. Show that its acceleration is about 0.8 m s^-2.

questions.question: The ball (mass 0.18 g) accelerates at about 0.8 m s^-2 under the electric force between the strips. Deduce whether this electric force is the only force acting to accelerate the ball.
questions.answer: No: the electric force alone would give about 1.0 m s^-2, more than the 0.8 m s^-2 observed, so another force (such as friction or air resistance) opposes the motion.
steps: Acceleration from the electric force alone: a = F / m = 1.8 x 10^-4 / 1.8 x 10^-4 = 1.0 m s^-2.
Observed acceleration is 0.8 m s^-2, so the net force is 1.8 x 10^-4 x 0.8 = 1.4 x 10^-4 N, which is less than 1.8 x 10^-4 N.
Therefore another force, such as friction or air resistance, opposes the motion, and the electric force is not the only force.

questions.question: Explain why the lengths of the drift tubes in a linac are not constant, unlike the lengths in the model.
questions.answer: The particles speed up in a linac, so each tube must be longer to keep the time in it equal to half the fixed a.c. period.
steps: In a linac the particle speed increases after each gap.
The time in each tube must equal half the period of the fixed-frequency a.c. supply.
Time = length / speed, so the length must increase as the speed increases.
The model has constant lengths because its ball does not speed up in the same way.

questions.question: Which statement about a cyclotron is NOT correct? A: magnetic field is at right angles to velocity; B: magnetic fields in dees keep particles in circles; C: particles accelerated by electric fields between dees; D: particles accelerated by electric fields inside dees.
questions.answer: D: the particles are accelerated by electric fields inside the dees
steps: A is correct: the magnetic force acts at right angles to velocity.
B is correct: the magnetic field in the dees gives the centripetal force.
C is correct: the electric field acts only in the gap between the dees.
D is incorrect: there is no electric field inside the dees, which are field-free.

questions.question: A proton enters a magnetic field perpendicular to its motion with speed v and follows a circle of radius r. Its radius then decreases. Which is a reason? A: kinetic energy decreases; B: magnetic flux density decreases; C: mass increases; D: momentum increases.
questions.answer: A: the kinetic energy of the particle decreases
steps: The radius of the path is r = m v / (B q) = p / (B q).
A decrease in r needs a decrease in momentum p, or an increase in B.
A decrease in kinetic energy means a lower speed, so the radius decreases; option A is correct.
A decrease in B would increase r, and an increase in momentum would also increase r.

questions.question: An alpha particle moving in a straight line with the same speed v enters the same magnetic field as the proton of Q25 and follows a circular path. Which is its initial radius? (Options A-D are not in the text.)
questions.answer: Pending: the options A-D are missing from the text. Physics gives r = m v / (B q), so the alpha radius is about twice the proton radius (mass about 4 times, charge 2 times).

questions.question: Which statement is true for charged particles in a cyclotron? A: accelerated by electric and magnetic fields; B: circular paths of constant radius; C: electric field changes direction in the gap between dees; D: magnetic field changes direction in the gap.
questions.answer: C: the electric field changes direction when the particles are in the gap between the dees
steps: Particles are accelerated only by the electric field in the gaps, so A is false.
The radius increases as particles gain speed, so B is false.
The alternating p.d. reverses the electric field direction in the gap, so C is true.
The magnetic field has a fixed direction, so D is false.

questions.question: Calculate the time a proton spends in one dee of a cyclotron with B = 0.55 T.
questions.answer: Time = 6.0 x 10^-8 s
steps: The proton moves in a half circle inside each dee, which takes half the period.
Time in one dee = T / 2 = pi m / (B q) = 5.96 x 10^-8 s, about 6.0 x 10^-8 s.
The mass 1.67 x 10^-27 kg is the standard proton mass (not printed in the text).

questions.question: Explain how the cyclotron increases the energy of the protons, referring to the alternating p.d. and the magnetic field.
questions.answer: The magnetic field keeps protons in circular paths inside the dees; the alternating p.d. in the gap accelerates them once per half turn, so their radius and energy increase.
steps: Inside the dees there is no electric field; the magnetic field B q v provides the centripetal force for the circular path.
The alternating p.d. across the gap between the dees produces an electric field across the gap.
The protons are accelerated across the gap each time they cross it, gaining q V each crossing.
The frequency of the p.d. matches the cyclotron frequency f = B q / (2 pi m), which is independent of speed.
The field reverses each half cycle, so the proton is accelerated every time it crosses the gap.
Each acceleration raises the speed, so the radius r = m v / (B q) increases and the proton spirals outward to higher energy.

questions.question: A bubble chamber shows a particle track. Which is a valid conclusion? A: negatively charged; B: moving from X to Y; C: speed increasing; D: experiences a centripetal force.
questions.answer: Pending: the particle track shown in the bubble chamber diagram is not in the text.

questions.question: In high-energy collisions electrons investigate nucleon structure. Which is the reason electrons need very high energy? A: so that new particles are created; B: so collisions are elastic; C: so electrons have a large wavelength; D: so a quark is knocked out.
questions.answer: A: so that new particles are created
steps: Mass can be created from kinetic energy by E = m c^2 in high-energy collisions.
High energy is therefore needed to create new particles.
A short (not large) wavelength is needed, so C is wrong; B and D are not the reason for the energy.

questions.question: Explain how a linac and a cyclotron use a potential difference to accelerate charged particles.
questions.answer: Both use an a.c. p.d. across gaps to give charged particles energy q V per crossing; the linac uses a line of tubes, the cyclotron uses a magnetic field to return particles to the gap.
steps: In both machines the particle gains energy q V each time it crosses a gap where the p.d. acts.
The field is shielded (zero) inside the drift tubes (linac) or the dees (cyclotron), so the particle moves at constant speed there.
Linac: the tubes are arranged in a line, and their lengths increase so each half period is matched to the particle's speed.
Cyclotron: the magnetic field bends the particle into a circle so it returns to the same gap each half turn.
The a.c. p.d. reverses in step with the particle's arrival, so it accelerates every time it crosses a gap.
The speed and radius increase with each acceleration, so the particle gains high kinetic energy.

questions.question: A linac applies 0.40 MV across each of 4 gaps to protons starting from rest. Show that the speed of the protons leaving the 4th gap is about 2 x 10^7 m s^-1.
steps: Energy gained per gap: q V = 1.6 x 10^-19 x 0.40 x 10^6 = 6.4 x 10^-14 J.
Energy after 4 gaps: E k = 4 x 6.4 x 10^-14 = 2.56 x 10^-13 J.
Speed from E k = 0.5 m v^2: v = sqrt(2 E k / m) = sqrt(2 x 2.56 x 10^-13 / 1.67 x 10^-27).
v = sqrt(3.07 x 10^14) = 1.75 x 10^7 m s^-1, which rounds to about 2 x 10^7 m s^-1.
Proton mass 1.67 x 10^-27 kg is the standard value (not printed in the text).

questions.question: In the cyclotron the protons leave when their path radius is 29 cm, with B = 0.55 T. Deduce whether their speed equals the speed leaving the 4th gap of the linac.
questions.answer: Cyclotron exit speed is about 1.5 x 10^7 m s^-1, which is less than the linac value of about 1.75 x 10^7 m s^-1, so the speeds are not the same.
steps: From B q v = m v^2 / r, the speed is v = B q r / m.
The linac exit speed from part (b)(i) is 1.75 x 10^7 m s^-1 (about 2 x 10^7 m s^-1).
The speeds are different, so the cyclotron protons are slower than the linac protons.
